newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW - H.I.S sees profit for airline.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - H.I.S sees profit for airline.

text.p: H.I.S Co Ltd, Japan's largest discount airline ticket seller, says its newly established domestic airline could turn a profit in the first year of operation.
"If possible we would like to make a profit in the first year of operation, although it is a big challenge," H.I.S. president Hideo Sawada told Reuters in a recent interview.

Sawada said the new airline, Skymark Airlines Co Ltd, would offer services in one of the country's busiest routes starting next summer, but did not specify which route. He said that it was still subject to change.

Skymark was established by H.I.S, Orix Corp, Hikari Tsushin Inc and Nomura Securities Co Ltd in November 1996 with the aim of fanning competition in the domestic airline sector, which has often been criticised by foreigners for its closeness, by offering cheap tickets.

Skymark will be one of the first airline companies to enter the highly profitable domestic aviation market in more than 40 years. A Skymark executive has said the firm will go public within five years and raise its capital by three billion yen to six billion yen by the time it actually begins services.
Sawada also said that H.I.S could be listed on a Japanese stock exchange, but added that no decision has been made.
"I think we could get listed anytime considering the scale of our operations and our achievements in terms of sales and profits, but I still have not decided whether to do so or not," he said.

H.I.S, which is presently registered on Japan's over-the-counter market, expects its parent current profit to surge by almost 23 percent to five billion yen in the year ending October 31, 1997, from an actual 4.07 billion yen a year earlier.
